problem: The sentence 'Only a few universities teach this advanced correction' is factually wrong. Curvature and refraction correction, and reciprocal levelling, are standard topics in every surveying syllabus and every standard textbook. A student reading this could wrongly skip the topic as optional.
fix: Delete the sentence. If a scope remark is wanted, write: 'The combined correction enters every levelling specification that allows long sights.'

problem: 'Two points A and B, distance d apart, share a level line' reads as if A and B are the same point or an undefined line. The student cannot tell that the derivation places both stations on the same level surface.
fix: Write: 'Two staff stations A and B lie on the same level surface, a distance d apart, so the curvature effect is the same at either end.'

problem: 'A value near 0.0673 d² is expected; a small leftover points to collimation error' is unclear — a reader can take 'small leftover' to mean a small value of ε itself, when the point is the excess over 0.0673 d².
fix: Write: 'ε should come out close to 0.0673 d², with d the long sight in km; any excess above that value is the collimation error of the instrument.'
